title: Indiana's 4th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for Indiana's 4th Congressional District pits Republican incumbent Rep. Jim Baird against Democratic nominee Drew Cox. The district covers 16 counties in west-central Indiana, including all of Tippecanoe County (home to Purdue University), and has been represented by Baird since 2019. The race is taking place in a heavily Republican district (Cook PVI R+18), where Baird has won each of his previous elections with over 64% of the vote. The primary elections on May 5, 2026 saw Baird defeat a primary challenger with 60.5% of the vote, while Cox emerged from an eight-candidate Democratic primary with 30.3%.
polling_note: No independent public opinion polls were found for the Indiana's 4th Congressional District general election as of mid-2026. The district is rated as safely Republican by major nonpartisan forecasters.

candidates.name: Jim Baird
candidates.summary: Jim Baird is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Indiana's 4th Congressional District, first elected in 2018. A Vietnam War veteran who earned a Bronze Star with V device and two Purple Hearts, Baird is a Purdue University graduate with a PhD in animal science from the University of Kentucky. He previously served in the Indiana House of Representatives (2010-2018) and as a Putnam County Commissioner, and sits on the House Agriculture, Foreign Affairs, and Science, Space, and Technology Committees.

candidates.name: Drew Cox
candidates.summary: Drew Cox is the Democratic nominee for Indiana's 4th Congressional District and a U.S. Marine Corps veteran. He is a visiting instructor in music at Purdue University, holding a doctorate in music, and has described his campaign as focused on ending political corruption, protecting workers' rights, expanding healthcare accessibility, and supporting veterans. Cox won a competitive eight-candidate Democratic primary on May 6, 2026 with 30.3% of the vote, and has pledged not to accept corporate PAC donations.
